deviation_mechanism: In a 24-layer dielectric stack, total reflectance depends on precise phase matching across interfaces. Small perturbations in individual layer thicknesses (order of 1-2 nm) shift the optical path length, breaking quarter-wave resonance conditions and inducing destructive interference between reflected wavefronts. The score depression in rounds 3–4 occurred because the optimization parameters stepped into thickness configurations that caused phase mismatch, lowering constructive interference. The sharp drop in valid candidates to 9 signifies that the optimization is colliding with hard geometric or manufacturing bounds, actively pruning any intermediate designs that briefly crossed into infeasible thickness regimes during the interference disruption.
